recipe: Stop recomputing long prompts: KV offload to RAM and NVMe, and sleep mode instead of a kill
note: Every entry is a transcription made by the studio. The basis field is the studio's original wording; read it with the label in the recipe: an entry without a published raw file is REPORTED, whatever its basis says.

receipts.claim: Baseline: second revisit pass over 2.7 M prompt tokens (34 long sessions), no offload, staged engine on the second card
receipts.value: revisit wall 1,687 s; 1,614 prompt tokens/s; 4% local cache hits; TTFT p50 295.1 s, p95 587.3 s; 185.8 kJ of GPU energy per million tokens; peak 81 C; average 300 W; KV pool 452,794 tokens
receipts.caveat: Synthetic token-id replay with idealised revisits; one run; staging card (cooler than the serving card). The baseline has a single revisit round.

receipts.claim: Same revisit pass with a 112 GiB RAM tier
receipts.value: revisit wall 80 s then 77 s; 34,238 / 35,855 prompt tokens/s; tier hit rate 96.3% / 96.0%; TTFT p50 12.6 / 14.9 s; 8.4 / 8.1 kJ per million tokens; peak 80 C
receipts.caveat: One run per round. Engine start took 103-122 s because the buffer is allocated and pinned. The shared-memory filesystem caps a RAM tier near 117 GiB.

receipts.claim: Same revisit pass with a 48 GiB RAM tier and NVMe behind it, clean start
receipts.value: revisit wall 78 s then 77 s; 34,792 / 35,624 prompt tokens/s; tier hit rate 96.2% / 96.0%; TTFT p50 12.8 / 16.0 s; 8.4 / 8.2 kJ per million tokens; peak 79 C
receipts.caveat: One run per round, from an empty NVMe directory and a cleaned shared-memory filesystem. Equals the 112 GiB RAM-only result at a smaller RAM footprint.

receipts.claim: Tiers smaller than the working set
receipts.value: RAM 64 GiB: revisit 1,314 s then 850 s, hits 26.9% / 43.1%, 144.7 / 92.8 kJ per million tokens; RAM 16 GiB + NVMe: 356 s then 522 s, hits 79.9% / 69.5%, 39.0 / 56.8 kJ per million tokens
receipts.caveat: The working set is about 93 GB of KV. Hit rates depend on least-recently-used eviction under shuffled revisits. One run each.

receipts.claim: First-touch prefill is unchanged by offload
receipts.value: about 1,668-1,676 s for 2.7 M tokens at about 1,612-1,620 prompt tokens/s in every configuration; 300 W average; peak 80-81 C; about 185 kJ per million tokens
receipts.caveat: Offload removes recomputation; it does not speed up the initial computation of a prompt.

receipts.value: text hashes of three probe prompts (20k, 60k, 120k tokens; 24 output tokens; temperature 0) identical across the baseline, the 112 GiB run and the tier runs, and identical between the cold pass and the later pass served from the tier; first-token log-probabilities differ by up to about 0.1 between separate engine runs
receipts.caveat: Three prompts, text-only replay; a long-horizon quality evaluation was not run. The log-probability difference is run-to-run jitter, not shown to be caused by offload.

receipts.claim: NVMe tier survives an engine restart
receipts.value: a second run reusing the NVMe directory after a restart served the whole 2.7 M-token working set at about 41,252 prompt tokens/s with a 97% hit rate in 66 s, against 1,668 s cold
receipts.caveat: An accidental second run, not a planned one; one run.

receipts.claim: Engine start time against tier size
receipts.value: 56 s with no tier; 59-71 s for 8-64 GiB; 103-122 s for 112 GiB
receipts.caveat: Warm compile cache; one start each.

receipts.claim: Transfer rate and KV size per token
receipts.value: 96 GB moved CPU to GPU in about 78 s (about 1.2 GB/s average), under the PCIe link rate and the drive's measured 13.9 GB/s direct read and 8.3 GB/s write; 33-34 KiB per token; a first-touch pass wrote 93 GB
receipts.caveat: Where the limit sits inside the engine is UNKNOWN. The per-token figure is arithmetic from the layer layout plus linear-attention state.

receipts.claim: Thermal scheduler with the offload connector
receipts.value: the lab's scheduler refused any external KV connector at the initial offload boot; a staging copy without the refusal ran with the governor forced to pause at 77 C and resume at 74 C: 10 pause and resume cycles while serving through the CPU tier, 0 errors, cold and late outputs identical
receipts.caveat: One staging run. The production change (allow the native offload connector alone, refuse every other) has 6 unit tests that pass; it was not exercised in service.

receipts.claim: Sleep mode on a staged engine with MTP, fp8 KV, vision, graphs and the thermal scheduler
receipts.value: level 1 sleep 0.67-0.70 s (initial call 7.8-10.8 s); wake 0.74-0.90 s; initial request after wake 0.07 s; card memory 73,939 MiB awake and 27,878 MiB asleep; level 2 sleep 0.14 s and total wake 4.3-4.7 s; text, image and 30k-token answers identical after 3 of 3 level-1 cycles and the level-2 cycle; works with a 32 GiB CPU tier (tier buffer survives sleep); kill-and-boot comparison about 55 s
receipts.caveat: One staged engine, three cycles. The second language model's sleep was not tested.

receipts.value: shared-memory filesystem caps the RAM tier (126 GiB, half of RAM): 128 GiB and 180 GiB tiers refused to start, 112 GiB worked; the NVMe tier leaks its RAM buffer after a kill; the NVMe tier has no size limit in vLLM 0.32.0; a quota janitor held a 12 GiB quota at 10.8-11.8 GiB with 0 engine errors
receipts.caveat: The janitor test fitted inside the GPU pool, so no tier loads happened while files were deleted: concurrent delete-during-load is UNKNOWN.

receipts.claim: Production state of the offload plan
receipts.value: prepared and dry-run; nothing executed on a serving engine; promotion on HOLD
receipts.caveat: Read from the plan documents and the squad state record of 2026-11-08 (offload held). A promotion would need one restart of the serving engine.

receipts.claim: What this recipe does not show
receipts.value: real revisit rate and working-set size; repeat runs; LMCache; sleep mode on the second language model; delete-during-load; long-horizon quality; any serving-card measurement
receipts.caveat: Listed so the 20x is not read as a service result.
